_comment_profile: NO `model` KEY, ON PURPOSE (24/09/2026 — ADR-026). A pin written here cannot win: server-managed settings, cached in <config_dir>/remote-settings.json, outrank every local file and are re-fetched at startup — a local edit to that cache was reverted the same morning it was made. And the pin this file used to carry was invisible: `opus[1m]` reads as a window choice and behaves as a version pin, because the 1M variant existed only for the previous Opus, so every session was born on it while the catalog already offered the newer one. To pin a model here again, NAME the version — "model": "opus55" — never a bare alias plus a window suffix. CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL stays `opus` on purpose: a subagent follows the newest Opus, not the session's pick. The highest effortLevel a settings FILE accepts is 'xhigh' — writing 'max' here silently does nothing; use /effort max for a single session.

permissions._comment: This repository holds documentation, shell hooks and templates — no application, no database, no secret. The allow-list is therefore reading, writing and git; nothing builds here. GRANTING A NEW PERMISSION IS THE OWNER'S ACT: it gets written into this file together with its reason and how to revert it, never applied silently. THE DENY-LIST ALWAYS BEATS THE ALLOW-LIST. ADR-019 GRANT (05/09/2026): the four read-only `gh` entries — `repo view`, `pr list`, `issue list`, `api repos/` — exist because the guest clause requires reading an upstream's language before we write into it, and a rule that prompts on every check is a rule that gets skipped. They read; they change nothing. To revert, delete those four lines: the clause then still applies, it just asks each time. `gh repo edit` and `gh repo delete` stay in `ask` and the deny-list still wins.
